meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'When you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it'?
meta.ogDescription: Paulo Coelho, in The Alchemist (1988). Wikiquote sources it to p. 22 with the Portuguese original — and notes the Emerson version is a later reworking.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: b. 1947 · Brazilian novelist, author of The Alchemist
answer.sourceLine: This is the real one. It comes from The Alchemist — O Alquimista, published in Portuguese in 1988 and in English in 1993 — and Wikiquote’s sourced entry places it at page 22, printing the Portuguese original beside it: “E quando você quer alguma coisa, todo o Universo conspira para que você realize seu desejo.” It matters because a reworded descendant of this sentence, “Once you make a decision, the universe conspires to make it happen”, circulates under Ralph Waldo Emerson’s name, and Emerson had nothing to do with it.

source.excerpt: When you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it.
trail: Wikiquote’s Coelho page gives the line in its sourced section for The Alchemist (1988) at p. 22 ↗, with the Portuguese original directly above it. The same entry records that a variant — “Once you make a decision, the universe conspires to make it happen” — has become attributed to Ralph Waldo Emerson, and that no occurrence of that statement has been located prior to The Gift of Depression (2001) by John F. Brown, p. 56.

Wikipedia confirms the work independently ↗: a novel by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho, first published in Portuguese in 1988 by Rocco, English release 1993 via HarperCollins, since translated into more than 65 languages.

Coelho has restated the idea in his own words since. Wikiquote records a list he published as “My 25 most important points” (3 September 2014) ↗ whose first item reads “When you want something, the whole universe conspires to make it happen…” — the author’s own later phrasing, closer to the popular form. We cite this as Wikiquote records it: the foundation page it links to was unreachable from this network, so we have not read it directly.

We could not check the sentence against a scan of the book. The English editions on the Internet Archive are lending-restricted and their full text cannot be searched, so the page number here is Wikiquote’s locator, offered as such rather than as a claim we confirmed ourselves.
source.excerptNote: The published English wording as Wikiquote gives it, at p. 22. Wikiquote prints the Portuguese original on the line above: “E quando você quer alguma coisa, todo o Universo conspira para que você realize seu desejo.” Note the trigger in both languages is wanting — quer — which is precisely what the popular “Emerson” rewrite changes to deciding.

source.rightsHolder: Paulo Coelho; English translation published by HarperCollins
source.rightsNote: The Portuguese original dates from 1988 and the English translation from 1993, so both the novel and the translation are in copyright in the United States — a translation carries its own rights, separate from the original. Nothing about the line’s ubiquity on social media changes that, and the fact that a reworded version travels under a 19th-century name does not make any version public domain. Quoted here briefly for identification and commentary.

author.name: Paulo Coelho
author.heading: About Paulo Coelho
author.bio: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist whose 1988 fable O Alquimista — The Alchemist in English from 1993 — became one of the best-selling books ever written. Its promise that the universe conspires to help someone pursuing their Personal Legend is the book’s signature idea and its most quoted sentence. It is also the seed of a family of paraphrases now floating free of the novel, several of which have been re-credited to older and more “quotable” names.

misattribution.heading: The line that got re-credited to Emerson
misattribution.intro: This sentence is the ancestor of one of the internet’s tidier fabrications. Reworded and handed to Ralph Waldo Emerson, it acquired the authority of a 19th-century essayist — the classic prestige transfer, and the reason the original is worth pinning down.

items.who: Ralph Waldo Emerson — “Once you make a decision, the universe conspires to make it happen”
items.why: Wikiquote records that no occurrence of the statement has been located before 2001 ↗, in The Gift of Depression by John F. Brown, p. 56 — 119 years after Emerson died. It also changes the meaning: Coelho’s condition is wanting something; the rewrite makes it deciding.

misattribution.truthLine: The thought is Coelho’s and dates from 1988. Emerson’s name was attached to a reworded copy more than a century after his death ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentence is the engine of The Alchemist. Santiago is told early that wanting something sincerely enough enlists the world on his side, and the rest of the novel tests that promise. Detached from the story it becomes a flat guarantee about the universe, which is roughly how it now circulates — and a large part of why the book is both beloved and derided.

It also shows how a quotation mutates. The wording drifted, the condition changed from wanting to deciding, and the new version needed a more venerable author than a living Brazilian novelist. Emerson supplied one. The original is younger, better sourced, and says something slightly different.
context.pull: Coelho’s condition is wanting. The Emerson rewrite makes it deciding — a different promise entirely.
